channel.title: Glossary on CCASH — Tokenize Your Community
channel.description: Recent content in Glossary on CCASH — Tokenize Your Community

item.title: AML (Anti-Money Laundering) - Glossary
item.description: AML (Anti-Money Laundering) refers to the laws, regulations, and procedures that prevent criminals from disguising illegally obtained funds as legitimate income. CCASH provides AML compliance infrastructure — transaction monitoring, sanctions screening, and suspicious activity reporting — for every community token economy on the platform.

item.title: Atomic Settlement - Glossary
item.description: Atomic Settlement is the simultaneous exchange of assets and payment in a single transaction — neither side can fail without the other. This ensures that token transfers and payments settle together or not at all.

item.title: Audit Trail - Glossary
item.description: An Audit Trail is a chronological record of every action in a system. CCASH provides a cryptographic audit trail for all token economy operations — every transaction, governance vote, and configuration change is signed and recorded. The trail is continuous from the shared platform through self-hosted graduation.

item.title: Bankable - Glossary
item.description: Bankable refers to assets or operations that can be integrated with traditional banking infrastructure. CCASH provides bankable token economies through its regulated MSB infrastructure, enabling fiat on-ramps, off-ramps, and settlement.

item.title: BLOOM - Glossary
item.description: BLOOM is an identity verification specification that CCASH implements for KYC/KYB workflows. It defines a state-machine approach to identity verification where each step is logged and irreversible.

item.title: Broker-Dealer - Glossary
item.description: A Broker-Dealer is a financial intermediary that buys and sells securities on behalf of clients or its own account. In the CCASH ecosystem, brokers and introducers can partner with operators to expand token economies.

item.title: Cap Table - Glossary
item.description: A Cap Table (Capitalization Table) is a record showing ownership stakes in an entity. In tokenized form, a cap table becomes transparent, programmable, and automatically updated with every token transfer — eliminating reconciliation and manual record-keeping.

item.title: Cap'n Proto - Glossary
item.description: Cap’n Proto is a zero-copy serialization protocol — data is read directly from the wire format with no encoding or decoding step. CCASH uses Cap’n Proto for inter-grain RPC communication, enabling native Sandstorm integration without an HTTP bridge.

item.title: Capability Security - Glossary
item.description: Capability Security is a model where access is granted through unforgeable tokens (capabilities) rather than identity-based permissions. CCASH uses capability security at every level — from inter-grain communication to user access control — ensuring least-privilege access throughout the platform.

item.title: Community Token - Glossary
item.description: A Community Token is a digital token that represents membership, access, or value within a specific community. CCASH enables creators, celebrities, sports clubs, brands, and family offices to launch their own community token economies — starting on the shared platform and graduating to self-hosted when they grow.

item.title: Compliance - Glossary
item.description: Compliance means adhering to the legal and regulatory requirements that apply to your operations. CCASH provides built-in compliance infrastructure — identity verification, transaction monitoring, audit trails, and reporting — for every community token economy on the platform, whether on the shared platform or a self-hosted instance.

item.title: Compliance Framework - Glossary
item.description:
Full Definition

The compliance framework within the CCASH platform consists of policies and procedures covering customer identification and verification, customer due diligence, transaction monitoring, sanctions screening, and reporting obligations. These policies form the foundation of the legal infrastructure layer and are enforced through the technology platform's governance tooling.

item.title: Coupon - Glossary
item.description: A Coupon is a periodic payment to token holders, similar to interest on a bond. CCASH supports automated coupon distributions through smart contracts for token economies that include regular yield or reward payments.

item.title: Custody - Glossary
item.description: Custody is the safekeeping of assets on behalf of token holders. CCASH provides custody infrastructure through its capability-secured grain architecture, with multi-party controls and cryptographic audit trails. Whether on the shared platform or a self-hosted instance, asset custody follows the same security model.

item.title: Data Sovereignty - Glossary
item.description: Data Sovereignty means that your community’s data belongs to you and stays under your control. On the shared platform, your data is isolated from other participants. When you graduate to a self-hosted instance, your data transfers completely — no gaps, no copies left behind, no ongoing access by CCASH.

item.title: Distributions - Glossary
item.description: Distributions are payments to token holders — revenue shares, dividend equivalents, or reward payouts. CCASH enables automated distributions through smart contracts, reducing administrative overhead and ensuring timely, accurate payments.

item.title: Entity Compartment - Glossary
item.description:
Full Definition

An entity compartment is a legally separate cell within the CCASH legal infrastructure structure, dedicated to a specific operator. Each compartment maintains its own records, assets, and liabilities, providing legal separation between operators. This structure ensures that the obligations of one operator do not affect the assets or operations of another.

item.title: Entity Framework - Glossary
item.description: The Entity Framework is CCASH’s set of pre-built legal structures — including Series LLC and other entity types — that provide legal isolation between operating compartments while maintaining operational efficiency. The framework is the legal foundation for the shared platform model.

item.title: Escrow - Glossary
item.description: Escrow refers to funds or assets held by a neutral party until specified conditions are met. CCASH supports escrow patterns for community token economies that require conditional releases, milestone-based payments, or dispute resolution mechanisms.

item.title: Fan Token - Glossary
item.description: A Fan Token is a type of community token used by celebrities, musicians, and sports clubs to connect directly with their audience. Fan tokens can gate exclusive content, voting rights, meet-and-greet access, digital collectibles, and more. Launch on CCASH’s shared platform. Graduate to your own branded instance when your fan economy grows.

item.title: Four-Eyes Principle - Glossary
item.description:
Full Definition

A governance requirement that certain critical actions must be approved by two distinct authorized signers before execution. Within the CCASH platform, four-eyes applies to high-tier transactions, customer verification final approval, override decisions on flagged items, refunds above threshold, and policy exception approvals. The requirement is enforced through the technology platform's cryptographic signature verification, ensuring that no single individual can authorize sensitive operations.

item.title: Framework Agreement - Glossary
item.description:
Full Definition

A framework agreement is a governing instrument executed at onboarding that establishes the legal terms under which an operator participates in the CCASH platform. It defines the rights, obligations, and operational parameters of the relationship, including provisions for growth, transition, and termination.

item.title: Governance Framework - Glossary
item.description: A Governance Framework defines how decisions are made within a token economy — who can propose changes, how voting works, and what authority different participants have. CCASH provides governance tooling from the shared platform through self-hosted graduation.

item.title: Governance Roles - Glossary
item.description:
Full Definition

Governance roles define the responsibilities, authorities, and limitations of each participant within the CCASH platform. The governance framework establishes supervisory roles with defined veto scope covering regulatory safety, intellectual property compliance, and operational integrity. Operational roles handle day-to-day management of services within the boundaries set by the governance framework.

item.title: Graduation Model - Glossary
item.description: The Graduation Model is CCASH’s core value proposition. Start your community token economy on our proven shared infrastructure — no development required, no infrastructure to manage. When your community grows, you graduate to your own self-hosted CCASH instance. Your brand, your data, your infrastructure. No lock-in, no platform risk. Your community, token data, and audit history transfer cleanly.

item.title: Grain - Glossary
item.description: A Grain is the fundamental isolation unit in the Sandstorm/Melusina operating system. Think of it as an indestructible, self-contained process that remembers everything. Each grain has its own append-only journal store, a set of capabilities granted to it, and an independent lifecycle. In CCASH, grains form the building blocks of both the shared platform and self-hosted instances.

item.title: Journal Store - Glossary
item.description: A Journal Store is an append-only encrypted log used by each grain for durable state storage. Every action is recorded in the journal, enabling deterministic replay for audit, forensic analysis, and disaster recovery. The journal is the foundation of CCASH’s tamper-evident audit trail.

item.title: K-Anonymity - Glossary
item.description: K-Anonymity is a privacy principle ensuring that individual data cannot be distinguished from at least k-1 other individuals in a dataset. CCASH applies k-anonymity to protect community member privacy in aggregate reporting.

item.title: KYC (Know Your Customer) - Glossary
item.description: KYC (Know Your Customer) is the regulatory process of verifying the identity of participants in a financial ecosystem. On CCASH, KYC workflows are built into the platform — whether you’re on the shared platform or a self-hosted instance. Operators configure identity verification requirements for their community token participants based on their specific regulatory obligations and risk profile.

item.title: Liquidity - Glossary
item.description: Liquidity refers to how easily a token can be bought or sold without affecting its price. Community token liquidity depends on the number of holders, trading volume, and market depth. CCASH supports liquidity-building mechanisms for growing token economies.

item.title: Loyalty Token - Glossary
item.description: A Loyalty Token reimagines traditional loyalty programs as token economies. Unlike traditional points that expire or get locked in, loyalty tokens can be traded, transferred, and governed by the community. Shopping centres, lifestyle brands, and retail destinations use CCASH to launch loyalty token programs — from cross-tenant rewards to visitor engagement.

item.title: Master NFT - Glossary
item.description: The Master NFT is the root authority in CCASH’s 4-layer NFT hierarchy. Controlled by threshold signing (requiring multiple key holders to agree), the Master NFT sits at the top of the chain of trust and can issue Reseller NFTs. It represents the sovereign authority for a CCASH deployment.

item.title: Maturity - Glossary
item.description: Maturity is the date when a token or financial instrument reaches the end of its term. At maturity, final distributions are made and the token may be redeemed or converted. CCASH supports maturity mechanics for token economies with defined time horizons.

item.title: Melusina - Glossary
item.description: Melusina is the capability-secured operating system and Sandstorm grain runtime that CCASH runs on. Melusina provides OS-level isolation for every component — each grain is a sandboxed application instance with its own journal store, capability set, and security boundary.

item.title: Membership Token - Glossary
item.description: A Membership Token represents ongoing membership in a community, club, or organisation. Access to member-only content, events, or governance decisions is gated by token ownership. Membership tokens can represent season tickets, club memberships, subscription access, or community participation rights.

item.title: Minimum Investment - Glossary
item.description: Minimum Investment is the smallest amount a participant can contribute to a token offering. CCASH supports configurable minimums per token economy, allowing creators to set participation thresholds that match their community’s profile.

item.title: NFT Hierarchy - Glossary
item.description: The NFT Hierarchy is CCASH’s 4-layer cryptographic chain of trust: Master NFT (root authority) → Reseller NFTs (delegated authority) → License NFTs (per-installation authority) → Share NFTs (per-domain access tokens). Every operation on the platform traces its authority back through this hierarchy. No NFT, no authority.

item.title: Offering - Glossary
item.description: An Offering is the process of making tokens available to a community. CCASH supports both public offerings (open to all verified community members) and private offerings (limited to specific groups), with compliance built into every distribution.

item.title: Offering Memorandum - Glossary
item.description: An Offering Memorandum is a legal document that describes the terms, risks, and structure of a token offering. CCASH provides template frameworks for offering documentation that can be customized for your community token economy.

item.title: On-Chain - Glossary
item.description: On-Chain refers to data or logic that exists and executes on a blockchain. CCASH uses on-chain compliance mechanisms — transfer hooks, authority verification, and audit trails — to enforce rules at the protocol level rather than relying on off-chain enforcement.

item.title: Operating Entity - Glossary
item.description:
Full Definition

An operating entity is a standalone legal entity owned and controlled by an operator within the CCASH platform. It holds the operator's brand, trade names, domains, intellectual property licenses, documentation, and operating manuals. The operating entity structure ensures that operators maintain clear ownership of their brand and operational assets while participating in the CCASH legal framework.

item.title: Operator - Glossary
item.description:
Full Definition

An operator is a participant that deploys the CCASH legal infrastructure and technology platform to serve customers under their own brand. Operators establish their operating entities within the CCASH framework and deploy branded instances of the technology platform. Each operator operates within defined governance roles and complies with the CCASH compliance framework policies.

item.title: PDA (Program Derived Address) - Glossary
item.description: A PDA (Program Derived Address) is an address on the Solana blockchain that is deterministically derived from program ID and seed data rather than being associated with a private key. PDAs are used in CCASH for on-chain compliance configuration storage.

item.title: Platform Disclaimer - Glossary
item.description:
Full Definition

CCASH's disclosure principle that all platform services are experimental in nature, carry inherent risk, and may produce unforeseen consequences. All participants must acknowledge these risks before using the CCASH platform. This disclosure ensures that operators and their customers engage with the platform with full awareness of its experimental character.

item.title: Platform Ecosystem - Glossary
item.description:
Full Definition

The platform ecosystem encompasses the complete network of operators, legal infrastructure, technology platform, and governance framework that constitutes CCASH. Operators deploy branded instances of the CCASH technology platform within the legal infrastructure, serving their own customers while benefiting from shared legal and technical foundations. The ecosystem is designed to support multiple operators with strong data isolation and clear role separation.

item.title: Platform User Roles - Glossary
item.description:
Full Definition

Platform user roles define the categories of participants within the CCASH ecosystem. Operators serve end-customers under their own brand, booking customer relationships into entity compartments. Each role carries defined rights, responsibilities, and access levels within the platform's governance framework.

item.title: Powerbox - Glossary
item.description: The Powerbox is CCASH’s inter-grain capability sharing mechanism. Instead of sharing passwords or API keys, grains offer capabilities to each other through the Powerbox. Capabilities are fine-grained, revocable, and auditable — ensuring least-privilege access at every level of a CCASH deployment.

item.title: Private Placement - Glossary
item.description: A Private Placement is a token offering made to a select group of qualified participants rather than the general public. CCASH supports private placement structures for community token economies that require participant qualification.

item.title: Professional Investor - Glossary
item.description: A Professional Investor is an individual or entity with sufficient expertise and experience to make independent investment decisions. CCASH supports professional investor qualification workflows for token economies that require participant accreditation.

item.title: Qualified Investor - Glossary
item.description: A Qualified Investor meets specific financial thresholds or professional criteria to participate in certain token offerings. CCASH provides verification workflows for qualified investor requirements in community token economies.

item.title: Regulated Operator - Glossary
item.description:
Full Definition

A regulated operator is a participant in the CCASH platform that provides financial services to customers under the CCASH legal infrastructure framework. Regulated operators operate within the compliance framework, adhering to policies covering customer identification, transaction monitoring, sanctions screening, and reporting obligations. The CCASH technology platform provides the tooling to support these compliance requirements.

item.title: Regulation D (Reg D) - Glossary
item.description: Regulation D (Reg D) is a US Securities and Exchange Commission regulation providing exemptions from registration for certain private offerings. CCASH supports Reg D-compliant structures for token economies that involve securities offerings.

item.title: Regulation S (Reg S) - Glossary
item.description: Regulation S (Reg S) is a US Securities and Exchange Commission regulation providing safe harbor for securities offerings made outside the United States. CCASH supports Reg S-compliant structures for international token economies.

item.title: Regulatory Framework - Glossary
item.description:
Full Definition

The regulatory framework encompasses the laws, regulations, and compliance requirements that govern financial services. CCASH provides legal infrastructure and technology platform tools designed to help operators establish and maintain compliant operations within their applicable regulatory environment.

item.title: Regulatory Framework - Glossary
item.description: A Regulatory Framework is the body of laws, regulations, and guidelines that govern financial operations. CCASH provides a comprehensive compliance framework that supports community token economies — from the shared platform to self-hosted instances.

item.title: Sandstorm - Glossary
item.description: Sandstorm is the open-source platform for self-hosted web applications that CCASH runs on. Each application runs in a sandboxed grain with its own data store, capability set, and security boundary — providing OS-level isolation for every component.

item.title: Scaling - Glossary
item.description:
Full Definition

Scaling refers to the process of growing an operation on the CCASH platform from initial deployment to full-scale operation. As operators grow their customer base, transaction volume, and operational footprint, they can expand their use of the CCASH legal infrastructure and technology platform. The platform is designed to accommodate growth without requiring operators to rebuild their infrastructure.

item.title: Security Token - Glossary
item.description: A Security Token is a digital token that represents ownership or entitlement to an underlying asset, subject to securities regulations. CCASH supports compliant security token issuance through its regulated MSB infrastructure.

item.title: Self-Hosted - Glossary
item.description: Self-hosted means running your own CCASH instance on your own infrastructure after graduating from the shared platform. Your brand, your data, your terms. No ongoing platform fees, no third-party dependency. The same CCASH platform you started with, now under your complete control. This is the destination of the graduation journey.

item.title: Series LLC - Glossary
item.description:
Full Definition

A limited liability company structure that allows the creation of legally separate compartments within a single LLC. Each compartment has its own assets, liabilities, and purposes, providing legal separation between different operations. This structure forms the foundation of the CCASH legal infrastructure, enabling multiple operators to maintain segregated operations within a unified framework.

item.title: Series LLC - Glossary
item.description: A Series LLC is a corporate structure that allows multiple segregated series to operate under a single LLC umbrella. Each series has its own assets, liabilities, and members — providing legal isolation while maintaining operational efficiency. This structure is the legal foundation for CCASH’s shared platform model.

item.title: Shared Platform - Glossary
item.description: The Shared Platform is CCASH’s multi-tenant infrastructure where community token economies launch before they graduate to self-hosted instances. It provides banking, compliance, and technology infrastructure that every participant shares — meaning you can launch your token economy in days, not months, without building any infrastructure yourself.

item.title: Smart Contract - Glossary
item.description: A Smart Contract is self-executing code that automatically enforces the rules of an agreement. In the CCASH ecosystem, smart contracts handle token issuance, transfers, compliance checks, and governance — powering the community token economies that operators launch on the platform.

item.title: SPV (Special Purpose Vehicle) - Glossary
item.description: An SPV (Special Purpose Vehicle) is a subsidiary entity created to isolate financial risk and hold specific assets separate from a parent. CCASH uses Series LLC architecture as a flexible alternative to traditional SPVs, providing legal isolation without the overhead of separate entity formation.

item.title: Threshold Signing - Glossary
item.description: Threshold Signing is a cryptographic scheme where a minimum number of independent signers must cooperate to produce a valid signature. No single party can act alone. CCASH uses threshold signing for high-authority operations — Master NFT control, governance decisions, and critical system parameters.

item.title: Tokenization - Glossary
item.description: Tokenization is the process of representing real-world assets, access rights, or community membership as digital tokens on a blockchain. CCASH enables community tokenization — allowing creators, celebrities, sports clubs, brands, and family offices to launch their own token economies.

item.title: Transfer Hook - Glossary
item.description: A Transfer Hook is an on-chain compliance mechanism that executes before any token transfer. The hook checks sender authorization, receiver eligibility, volume limits, and jurisdiction filters — denying non-compliant transfers at the protocol level. This ensures compliance is enforced, not just monitored.

item.title: Treasury Series - Glossary
item.description: A Treasury Series is a legal compartment within a Series LLC structure dedicated to managing treasury assets. In the CCASH ecosystem, treasury series can hold and manage the proceeds of token economies, providing legal isolation and clear audit trails.

item.title: Trustee - Glossary
item.description: A Trustee is an independent party who oversees compliance with governing documents and acts in participants’ interests. In the CCASH ecosystem, trustees can be configured as part of the governance framework for token economies that require independent oversight.

item.title: Waterfall - Glossary
item.description: A Waterfall is the order in which proceeds from a token economy are distributed among participants. CCASH supports programmable waterfalls through smart contracts — automating distribution according to rules defined by the token economy creator.

item.title: White-Label - Glossary
item.description: White-Label refers to operating a CCASH platform under your own brand. On the shared platform, your community sees your brand while CCASH provides the infrastructure. When you graduate to self-hosted, your brand operates on your own infrastructure. Your community never needs to know about CCASH unless you choose to tell them.
